elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.1 as rendered: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of ..." followed by "The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims." Unchanged favourable language retained.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 21.1 now reads "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000" — correct basis (paid or payable, not broader 'all amounts'), correct lookback anchor (preceding the claim) and correct floor. The lowercase 'fees' plus 'under this Agreement and all Order Forms' escapes the illusory defined term "Fees" (= USD 12,000 Implementation Fee) and the first-Order-Form limiter.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.2 retained verbatim: "neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill", with the Customer-favourable direct-damages sentence preserved.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims (carved out of the 21.1 cap by "Except for Excluded Claims") includes "a Party's breach of confidentiality ... obligations".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations" sits within Excluded Claims and therefore outside the 21.1 cap.
21.3: "its indemnification obligations" listed as an Excluded Claim; 21.1 and 21.2 both open "Except for Excluded Claims".
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" within Excluded Claims.
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" within Excluded Claims.
21.3: "... wilful misconduct, or fraud" within Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" within Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: 21.3 as rendered: "Customer's obligations to pay undisputed amounts due under this Agreement and any Order Form are not damages and are not limited by this Section." The narrow noun "Fees" (USD 12,000 Implementation Fee) and the "for conforming Services" limiter are gone, so the carve-out now reaches Customer payment obligations as a whole; the retained "undisputed" qualifier is a Customer-favourable restriction, not a subset-of-Fees defect. The deterministic check flagging this element appears to be keyed to the literal phrase "payment obligations" and does not reflect the substance of the rendered sentence.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.1: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... The cap is mutual".

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: 21.1 measures the cap by "fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim", with a USD 1,000,000 floor as the greater-of alternative.
21.3 Excluded Claims includes "its indemnification obligations"; 21.1 excepts Excluded Claims from the cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims includes "a Party's breach of confidentiality ... obligations".

reasons: Deviation finding is correct: as drafted, the cap was measured by the defined term "Fees" (1.5/1.6 = the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee) and further limited to "the first Order Form", making the mutual cap illusory and below six months' fees — walk-away territory notwithstanding the otherwise complete carve-out set.

Both edits are surgical and each is required by a preferred element: (i) resetting the 21.1 measure to lowercase fees under the Agreement and all Order Forms with the USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor and a lookback preceding the claim; (ii) broadening the 21.3 payment carve-out from "undisputed Fees for conforming Services" to "undisputed amounts due under this Agreement and any Order Form". No survival tails, expense language, procedures, or extra damages categories were added, and 21.2 (including the favourable direct-damages sentence) and the entire Excluded Claims list are retained verbatim.

Removal of "for conforming Services" is within the checklist rather than a gratuitous deletion: the element requires Customer payment obligations as a whole to sit outside capped damages, which a conforming-Services subset would not achieve. Retaining "undisputed" correctly preserves the existing Customer-favourable restriction.
Intent is preserved: the definitions at 1.5/1.6 are untouched so payment and invoicing provisions that use "Fees" continue to operate, and no cross-reference is left dangling.

Drafting refinement to consider (not a defect that blocks completion): because the Agreement defines capitalised "Fees" narrowly, a counterparty could argue lowercase "fees" in 21.1 still imports that definition. Consider adding "(whether or not constituting 'Fees' as defined)" or "all amounts payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms" wording in negotiation to close the ambiguity; as rendered, the lowercase usage plus "under this Agreement and all Order Forms" is sufficient on its face.
